evidence.quote: The as-cast Co23Cr23Ni23Mn31 (at.%) alloy was produced by melting pure Co, Cr, Ni and Mn metals (> 99.8 wt% purity) in a vacuum induction furnace.
The as-cast cubic ingot (10 × 30 × 60 mm3) was rolled by 50% in thickness at 1173 K.
Subsequently, the 5 mm-thick alloy sheets were homogenized at 1373 K for 2 h in the protective argon atmosphere, followed by immediate quenching in water.

evidence.quote: SAED pattern along the [011]f.c.c zone axis in Fig. 5 (c) identifies a monolayer of SFs on the (111) and (11 1) crystallographic planes.
The intersection activities of these SFs led to formation of Lomer-Cottrell locks (LCs).
As the engineering strain increased to 34%, the formation of multiple nanotwins (~several tens of nanometres) and their intersections became predominant in Fig. 5 (d).
In the present work, the SF regions developed into the h.c.p lamellaes at large strain value of 34%.
When the engineering strain reached 45%, the amorphous bands occurred in the f.c.c Co23Cr23Ni23Mn31 alloy matrix. The thickness of these amorphous bands was measured to be 20-70 nm.
Additionally, trace analysis of tensile samples suggests that the plastic deformation in Co23Cr23Ni23Mn31 corresponded to the high-density of dislocation walls (HDDWs).

The as-cast Co23Cr23Ni23Mn31 (at.%) alloy was produced by melting pure Co, Cr, Ni and Mn metals (> 99.8 wt% purity) in a vacuum induction furnace.
The as-cast cubic ingot (10 × 30 × 60 mm3) was rolled by 50% in thickness at 1173 K.
Subsequently, the 5 mm-thick alloy sheets were homogenized at 1373 K for 2 h in the protective argon atmosphere, followed by immediate quenching in water.
To obtain samples with fine-grained structures, the homogenized alloy was further cold-rolled from 5 mm to 2.5 mm in thickness at 298 K.
Then, the cold-rolled samples were annealed at 1173 K in Ar atmosphere for 30 min before water quenching.
XRD patterns in Fig. 1 (c) verified that the as-cast alloy consists of only f.c.c crystal structure.
Many microscale annealing twins (~100 μm) were observed.
Fig. 2 (a) represents the pseudo 3D microstructure of as-deformed Co23Cr23Ni23Mn31 alloy, having full equiaxed or nearly-equiaxed grains with an average grain size of 13.12 μm.
Nearly, every microvoid contains a nanoparticle, as highlighted by the white arrows in Fig. 4 (a).
